t_dead_flip.unit: s: the largest t_dead at which the named gain beats gain 50, per % of stars clipped
t_dead_flip.note: uncertainty is the t_dead grid step only.  Set by the end of the sub-length grid (600 s), not by the physics, at 10%: gain 50's best sub there is the grid's last.  model predictions, nothing measured.  31's curve (pareto_curve.csv) with t_dead swept 0-31.46 s in 0.1 s steps; clipping read from it unchanged, SNR in plane B recomputed with model.snr_sub and model.subs_in over a 4.42 h night and checked against 31's snr_B to 1e-06.  eta_comb = 1.0, as agreed for 31, and never measured at any cadence but every frame: dithering less can only lose more to stacking, so every flip here is the most favourable case for the higher gain.  Gains (50, 100, 200), sub lengths 10-600 s on 31's grid; NGC 7000, 2026-09-05

dither_cadence_flip.unit: frames per dither needed to reach t_dead_flip, per % clipped, per download value
dither_cadence_flip.note: t_dead(k) = download + (t_dead - download) / k, with t_dead 31.46 s.  The split is t_dead_decomposition's, INFERRED and not measured: 'archive' is the historic corpus's 0.68 s, not ours; 'bound' is 7.99 s, the shortest gap of our night and only an upper bound.  Rounded up: dithering every k-th frame or less often reaches the flip, more often does not.  model predictions, nothing measured.  31's curve (pareto_curve.csv) with t_dead swept 0-31.46 s in 0.1 s steps; clipping read from it unchanged, SNR in plane B recomputed with model.snr_sub and model.subs_in over a 4.42 h night and checked against 31's snr_B to 1e-06.  eta_comb = 1.0, as agreed for 31, and never measured at any cadence but every frame: dithering less can only lose more to stacking, so every flip here is the most favourable case for the higher gain.
